workflow.title: One task → many helpers
workflow.summary: Split the goal across many agents
workflow.detail: An orchestrator splits the goal into independent pieces and hands each to its own AI agent — many run at the same time.

workflow.title: Each agent works in isolation
workflow.summary: Each agent works on its own copy
workflow.detail: Every agent takes a separate copy of the code so they never step on each other's work.

workflow.title: Small, scoped changes
workflow.summary: Small steps, not one big change
workflow.detail: Work lands in small, reviewable steps instead of one big risky change.

workflow.title: The gate
workflow.summary: Analysis + full tests, or it stops
workflow.detail: Before anything can land it must pass automatic checks — code analysis plus the full test suite. A failure stops it cold.

workflow.title: Land on dev
workflow.detail: Only work that passed the gate joins the shared dev line. main only ever moves forward from dev, on a deliberate promote.

workflow.title: Auto-deploy
workflow.summary: A promote to main deploys itself
workflow.detail: Once promoted to main, the change publishes to the live web app automatically — no manual deploy step.

workflow.title: Version stamp
workflow.summary: Every build is dated and traceable
workflow.detail: Each build records its date, time and id, so you can always see exactly what's live (Account → View app version).

updates.title: Faster scrolling through long reads
updates.summary: Engine · a fast-scroll edge strip jumps you through a long article instead of endless flicking.
updates.detail: A draggable strip along the right edge of any long read (Wikipick's article reader is first) lets you jump anywhere in the document — drag it and a floating bubble shows which section you're passing. It fades away when you're not using it, so it never gets in the way of reading.

updates.title: One consistent spacing rhythm
updates.summary: App · buttons, cards, and sections space themselves the same way everywhere.
updates.detail: The launcher, appearance, about, release-status, store, and get-the-app screens now share one spacing standard instead of each screen inventing its own gaps — and the overflow menu regrouped into clearer sections (Apps / Look / Your data / App).

updates.title: Popups instead of empty pages
updates.summary: Engine · short details now open in a small popup, not a mostly-empty full page.
updates.detail: Builds on the full-screen-push standard from late August: for a short detail — a couple of lines, not a whole document — a full page was mostly empty space. Those surfaces (this app's own What's-new cards, Claude-workflow steps, and System boards among them) now open a small centered popup instead, dismissed with a tap outside or the ×. Never a bottom sheet, either way.

updates.title: See your build
updates.detail: A version stamp inside the app plus a freshness file on the live site, so you can tell at a glance when it last changed.

updates.title: One tidy ⋮ menu
updates.detail: The home-screen header collapsed into a single overflow menu — store, appearance, account, version, and more.

updates.title: Action picker
updates.detail: Set what a button does by picking from menus — no JSON. Chain several steps with ‘+ then’.

updates.title: Automated rules (only if…)
updates.detail: Make the app react: when a condition is true, do one thing (and optionally something else otherwise).

updates.title: Process templates
updates.summary: Stamp out a saved task template
updates.detail: Save a task and its sub-steps as a template; tap to stamp out a fresh copy into your tasks.

updates.title: Visual condition builder
updates.detail: Build the ‘when…’ part of a rule with field / is / value rows — and/or/not — no typing JSON.

updates.title: Recurring tasks
updates.detail: Give a task a repeat (daily, weekly, monthly); completing it automatically creates the next one.

updates.title: Quick stage + undo
updates.summary: Tap to advance a task's stage
updates.detail: Tap a task to move it To do → Doing → Done (it stamps the date), with an Undo button.

updates.title: Share by code or file
updates.summary: Copy or export a whole app
updates.detail: Copy a whole app to your clipboard, or save it to a file — and paste/import it on another device.

updates.title: New building blocks
updates.detail: Reusable pieces added across apps: nested apps, a file explorer, compare & tier-list views, and more.

house_rules.name: No slide-up views
house_rules.statement: popup or navigation — slide up should not be so common
house_rules.detail: Detail views never slide up from the bottom. A small amount of detail opens as a popup over the current screen; anything substantial pushes to its own full-screen page. This applet is fully compliant. App-wide, a showModalBottomSheet inventory sweep is still open — other applets are migrated one at a time, not all at once.

house_rules.name: Tap opens, never expands
house_rules.detail: Tapping a row always opens its detail view (popup or push) — it never expands the row in place, and it never toggles. One tap, one predictable outcome, everywhere the engine renders a tappable row.

house_rules.name: Views tell a story, never flat lists
house_rules.statement: just a list that gives no visual direction of narrative
house_rules.detail: A screen that just enumerates rows leaves the visitor to guess at meaning. Views are designed with a shape that carries the story — a time spine, a flow of stages, a grouped structure — not a flat unordered list. What's-new (time spine) and Timeline (lanes across days) already carry this; more views are converted as they're touched.

house_rules.name: One spacing rhythm
house_rules.statement: one consistent spacing rhythm across the app
house_rules.detail: Every screen spaces itself from the same AppSpacing token set instead of inventing its own gaps — launcher, appearance, about, release-status, store, and get-the-app screens were the first sweep; the token set is now the only sanctioned way to space anything new.

house_rules.name: Entry views orient
house_rules.detail: The first screen a visitor lands on always carries a one-line purpose header — what this is, in plain words — before any data. The applet lint gates this as an ERROR now: an entry screen with no orienting header fails the gate, not just a style note.

house_rules.name: Design real-estate efficiency
house_rules.statement: condense, hide, expand — don't waste the screen
house_rules.detail: Screen space is scarce, phone-first. Prefer condensing, hiding behind a clear affordance, or expanding on demand over spreading content thin. Phone width (375px) is the acceptance test for every layout.

house_rules.name: Layout integrity: states never squeeze content
house_rules.statement: spacing tokens only; states never squeeze content; 375px one-line tests
house_rules.detail: Loading, empty, and error states reserve their own space — they never compress or reflow the real content around them. Every layout is checked at 375px for accidental wraps or overflow before it ships.

house_rules.name: House design rules — v1.1
house_rules.detail:
The full v1.1 rulebook, applied at design review before build and re-checked at 375px before any promote. Canonical copy kept in the team's internal rules doc. Origin: Parley product-polish arc + the user's 0901 direction.

1. Orient in About, not popups. Every applet has a standard ⓘ About section holding what-is-this and how-to; working screens stay clean — no floating banners. Check: ⓘ reachable from the top bar on every applet; no dismissible banner on any working screen.
2. Say it once. No screen delivers the same message twice in different clothes. Check: read every visible string aloud — no two say the same thing.
3. Space is content. No dead bands. Condense → hide → expand, in that order, before adding scroll. Check: at 375px, no empty region taller than 24px that isn't deliberate breathing room around a focal element.
4. Controls show state. A picker displays its current value, not its category — "English ▾", never "Language ▾". Check: no control labeled only by what it selects when a selection exists.
5. One accent, layered darks. Colors come from the applet's token set; the accent marks exactly: primary action, active destination, own contributions. Check: every fill traces to a token; accent in those three roles only.
6. Three text sizes per screen (app bar may add a fourth). Hierarchy from size + weight, not more sizes. Check: distinct body font sizes ≤ 4.
7. Popup or push, never slide-up. Tap opens detail as a centered dialog or full-screen push; bottom sheets are retired. Check: nothing slides from the bottom edge; every tap has one outcome.
8. Visible async. Every wait names what is happening and where it came from; no bare spinners. Check: any state > 1s carries a sentence; failures say what failed and what to do.
9. 44px targets, token spacing (4/8/12/16/24). Check: measure the smallest control; grep for off-scale values.
10. Examples say so, empties teach. Demo content is visibly labeled; an empty view states the next action. Check: seed rows carry an example marker; every empty state contains a verb.

house_rules.name: House design rules — v1.2
house_rules.statement: dense grabbable menus; one shared board grammar
house_rules.detail:
Two additions folding in the design-language work since v1.1.

11. Menus are dense and grabbable. One shared menu sheet everywhere: compact rows, groups separated by a hairline only, every item visible without scrolling at default height, a visible handle that both expands and dismisses. Check: no padded section band in any menu; the last item is visible with zero scroll; the handle does both.
12. Boards speak one grammar. Structural/system data views use a fenced-axes board: axes carry meaning, each fence owns its contents, a span is used only when one thing truly lives in both, rigid outside and organic inside, one page never mixes diagram styles. Check: every axis labeled; every span justified in one sentence; no second diagram style on the same surface.
